description: Editorial description of the on-screen teaching sequence; not spoken narration. The soundtrack is music.

segments.text: Attention creates a new representation for a position by mixing information from other positions.
A context-sensitive pronoun motivates the operation. This introductory illustration allows bidirectional context.
The worked example uses four token positions and small vectors so the calculation can be followed by hand.
Learned linear projections produce queries, keys and values from the input representations.
A query is compared with each key using a dot product. These comparisons form a row of attention scores.
Matrix multiplication QKᵀ computes scores for every query against every key.
Divide the scores by the square root of the key dimension to moderate their scale before softmax.
Apply softmax separately to each score row. The resulting weights are nonnegative and sum to one.
A larger score receives a larger weight relative to the other entries in that row.
Multiply each value vector by its weight and add the results to produce one output vector.
Repeating the operation for every query produces the output matrix: softmax(QKᵀ/√dₖ)V.
The output depends on both the learned projections and the current context. It is not simply a lookup of one word.
Causal masking will prevent a position from using future tokens when the task is next-token prediction.
Pause and trace a single query: compare keys, scale scores, normalize weights and mix values.
Recap the computation. The next animation adds masks, heads and position information.
